A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoCoEdit work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching material across pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, qualitative outputs, correlation analyses, and a user study involving 30 volunteers and 100 sampled images.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds perceptual-metric evaluations, dataset-size and SFT experiments, additional baseline comparisons, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The CoCoEdit rewards, positive and negative regional regularizers, optimization objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Expanded explanations of instruction refinement and mask usage do not establish a procedural change; SFT is an added comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the OmniEdit/ImgEdit-derived training coverage and GEdit-Bench/ImgEdit-Bench evaluations, including local and global editing tasks. The new 120K experiment changes training sample count without establishing a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands the comparisons with an SFT-on-40K control in Table 4 and FLUX.1-Fill-dev and ICEdit in Appendix C.4/Table 7. Existing model, RL, and commercial comparators remain. ICEdit was cited in v1 but was not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Tables 1–2 add LPIPS and DINO evaluation metrics. New Table 4 introduces 120K-versus-40K RL conditions and SFT using source ground-truth images with a non-edit-region PSNR/SSIM consistency loss. These extend the evaluation design; the original training and user-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of dataset-size sensitivity, SFT versus RL, and consistency under metrics excluded from the training reward, plus an efficiency comparison with Edit-R1. These address additional questions about sufficiency, attribution, and reward overfitting. The original component ablations, reward-ratio curves, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: The user-study sampling seed, participant information, and correlation-reporting practices remain unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, commercial-comparison, and component-ablation values are retained. v2 adds LPIPS/DINO scores, SFT/120K results, FLUX.1-Fill-dev/ICEdit results, and efficiency outcomes. For example, new Table 4 reports GEdit overall/PSNR values of 7.219/20.293 for SFT and 7.723/22.204 for 120K RL; these are additional conditions, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, definitions, assumptions, and regional-regularization derivations in Section 3 and Appendix B remain unchanged. The added empirical metrics introduce no new formal definitions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims: CoCoEdit improves content consistency while maintaining competitive editing, supported by the curated dataset and mask-augmented benchmarks. Additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that consistency gains extend beyond reward metrics, 40K samples suffice, and RL contributes more than the curated data alone. It explains SFT's weaker editing scores through unfiltered ground-truth quality and clarifies the existing ablation baseline. Appendix D's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.5 newly reports approximately 70 GB VRAM and per-step times of 10 minutes for Edit-R1 versus 12 for CoCoEdit. v2 also describes ground-truth retrieval and the consistency loss for the SFT control. Existing implementation settings, pseudocode, and the project link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to FireEdit and FLUX, and explicitly contrasts CoCoEdit's mask-free inference with spatially grounded editing. It also discusses the newly evaluated mask-guided and in-context alternatives. The main related-work survey and overall research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected method and experimental explanations, adds subheadings within the ablation discussion, introduces Section 4.5 and Appendix C.4, and replaces the preprint footer with proceedings information. Most prose and the overall document structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain LPIPS/DINO columns, and new Tables 4 and 7 display the added experiments. Existing tables are renumbered, and Figures 7, 13, and 14 move with text reflow. The figures themselves and the overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens an already substantial empirical evaluation with metrics outside the training reward, dataset-size/SFT controls, additional baselines, and compute-cost disclosure. These provide useful corroboration and context. However, the SFT comparison does not cleanly isolate algorithm effects because v2 acknowledges that its ground-truth targets were not filtered for SFT quality. The net gain is positive but incremental.
